entries.text: Gould’s only commercial organ recording stops at Contrapunctus IX: Volume I of an Art of Fugue that never continued. The approach is pianist’s counterpoint transferred to the organ, not a finished cycle. Against the Emersons’ complete quartet it is an incomplete experiment — interesting as documentary Gould. Keep it for Gould’s oddities, not as the Art of Fugue.

The Emersons play the Art of Fugue as a modern string quartet: clear voice colouring, unfinished Contrapunctus XIV left mid-phrase, deathbed chorale at the close. Against Gould’s unfinished organ Volume I this is a complete argument for open-score Bach heard as four strings. Clarity without mixed-ensemble colour fights. Référence on this shelf.
